list_latest_jobs.description: Read the board in the order it was posted, newest first, with no ranking and no filtering. This is the feed itself rather than a search of it, which makes it the step for the two things a search cannot do. To copy the board into a sheet or a database, feed each run's 'next_cursor' into the next run and it carries on exactly where the last one stopped, never repeating a job. For a scheduled digest, give it the moment the last run finished and it returns only what has appeared since, so an alert never repeats itself.

parameters.description: Only return jobs whose working hours overlap this UTC offset. This is the other half of whether a remote job is workable: a role open to your country can still expect you online at three in the morning. A job that states no timezone requirement is not returned when this is set, so leave it empty unless the hours matter. A job's own 'timezones' values, such as 'UTC+05:30', can be passed straight in.

The list names the companies posting right now, and any other can be typed in: Himalayas knows a company by a short name such as 'servicetitan', which is what every job returns as its 'company_slug'. parameters.description: Only return jobs whose published pay reaches this figure over a year. An hourly, weekly, fortnightly or monthly rate is converted to a year first, so an advertised 100 an hour counts as 208,000. The comparison is made in each job's own currency and no exchange rate is applied, because the API publishes none. Roughly one job in three publishes what it pays, and setting any figure here leaves out the rest, so leave it empty unless pay is the point.

description: Search Himalayas, the remote-only job board, through its free public API. One search covers everything the board knows about a job: the words in it, the country you can work from, whether it is open worldwide, the timezone it expects you in, the level, the employment type, the employer and what it pays. Read the board in posting order to copy it somewhere or to run a daily digest that never repeats itself, pull one job in full from its link, and see who is hiring. Every description arrives as plain text rather than HTML, and every job carries its pay written out and the link to apply. No account or API key is required.
